analysis:
Examined all supplied test source, patches and file metadata against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. No concrete regression is established by these test-only changes. GLM5NextProviderLoopTests.swift:194-217 adds assertions that managed loading avoids separate WeightHasher reads, publishes the manifest aggregate as the live hash, and persists a reusable record. Existing retirement/cancellation and reservation-unwind tests remain present. VerifiedWeightHashStoreTests.swift:44-102 covers model-ID separation, mode 0600, file-change invalidation despite restored mtime, added/appended files, malformed/schema-mismatched state, and GLM-only managed verification. StartupPreloadTests.swift's added head lines 300-314 check delivery of load/self-test errors to a scripted failure hook; the surrounding base tests already document self-test fail-open/fail-closed behavior, so that is not a new issue.
Integration must examine the changed production hash-store and managed-load consumers: whether the digest represents the exact loaded bytes, whether identity capture and later reuse resist substitution races, and whether operator-editable valid records can be mistaken for trusted verification (A-004, T-012, T-027, TB-003/TB-007). Mode 0600 alone does not authenticate state against the owning operator. The supplied tests do not establish those implementation contracts or any bypass. Also trace live registration and SSD weightHash binding under T-041; this GLM fixture disables the SSD cache at lines 38-46 and does not test that interaction. Verify production failure-hook handling preserves admission/retirement and avoids sensitive diagnostics; only stub errors are exercised here. No supplied change directly modifies encryption, attestation/authorization, billing, keys, media exposure or privileged-helper controls. These are local coverage limits, not a full-PR security conclusion.
